content_of_post_to_comment: If the Ivies stopped giving preferential treatment to children of rich parents, those children would be forced to seek education at a broader range of universities which would spread their network access to a broader swath of the country, help elite networks regain the pulse of the nation, and accelerate both dynamism and general productivity.
comment: The interesting tradeoff is that elite networks may gain national breadth, but only if opportunity—not just credential access—drives who gets included in those networks.
